definition_zh: 反叛者；武装反抗；抗拒常规
definition_en: a person who rises against authority; to rise against authority; to refuse accepted rules
core_image: 举着火把的人群背对王座站成一排
scene: 广场上人群举着火把，把印着徽章的旗帜倒转过来。 The rebel forces refused to surrender.
sceneCN: 这里 rebel 作定语，指「反叛者」（第 1 个义项：拿起武器反叛的人）；句意为叛军拒绝投降。画面里可留意：倒转的旗帜、背对王座的人群。

senses.title: A person who rises against authority
senses.definition: a person who takes up arms or openly refuses to obey those in power
senses.definitionCN: 拿起武器或公开拒绝服从当权者的人
senses.example: The rebel was arrested at dawn.
senses.exampleCN: 那名反叛者在黎明时被捕。
senses.why: The Latin rebellis meant one who renews war, and the noun kept that image of a person who reopens a fight.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 rebellis 意为重新开战的人，名词保留了「重新掀起战斗」这一意象。

senses.title: To rise against authority
senses.definition: to fight against a government or a ruling power
senses.definitionCN: 与政府或统治力量作战
senses.example: The peasants rebelled against the heavy taxes.
senses.exampleCN: 农民们反抗沉重的赋税。
senses.why: The verb was formed from the noun, turning the person who renews war into the act of renewing it.
senses.whyCN: 动词由名词而来，把「重新开战的人」转成了「重新开战」这一行为。

senses.title: To resist accepted rules
senses.definition: to refuse to accept the habits or rules of a group, often in a personal way
senses.definitionCN: 拒绝接受某个群体的习惯或规则，常带个人色彩
senses.example: Teenagers often rebel against their parents' advice.
senses.exampleCN: 青少年常常抗拒父母的建议。
senses.why: Rebellion moved from the battlefield into daily life, where refusing advice is a small war of one's own.
senses.whyCN: 反叛从战场走进日常生活，拒绝建议就是一个人自己的小战争。

intro.en: Rebel carries war inside it: a Latin word for war sits at its centre, joined to a prefix meaning again.
intro.cn: rebel 内部藏着战争：拉丁语的「战争」一词就在它中间，并与表「再次」的前缀相连。

items.en: Bellum meant war, the raw material of every rebellion.
items.cn: bellum 意为战争，是一切反叛的原材料。

items.en: The prefix re- added the idea of again or in return, giving renewed war.
items.cn: 前缀 re- 加上「再次」或「回击」的意思，构成「重新开战」。

items.en: Rebellis described both a renewed war and the person who waged it.
items.cn: rebellis 既指重新开战的战争，也指发动它的人。

items.en: Old French rebelle carried the person and the act into English.
items.cn: 古法语 rebelle 把人与其行为一起带入英语。

items.en: Modern English uses rebel for the person, for the act, and for a personal refusal of rules.
items.cn: 现代英语用 rebel 指人、指行为，也指个人对规则的抗拒。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers verbs and nouns close in spelling; the near-meaning group gathers words for armed and unarmed resistance.
note.cn: 形近组收拼写相近的动词与名词；近义组收表武装与非武装抵抗的词。

entries.definition: To drive back or push away.
To enjoy oneself loudly.
A blunt refusal.
One who rises in armed revolt.
To turn against authority.
To stand against force.
A soldier who refuses orders.

normalIntro.en: The word keeps the Latin word for war at its centre, so every sense carries a small battlefield.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词中间藏着拉丁语的「战争」，因此每个义项都带着一小片战场。

normal.en: Re plus bellum: making war again is the oldest picture of a rebel.
normal.cn: re 加 bellum：重新开战，就是 rebel 最古老的画面。

normal.en: A rebel can be a person or an act, so one spelling serves noun and verb.
normal.cn: rebel 既可指人也可指行为，同一拼写兼作名词与动词。

normal.en: The noun stress falls on the first syllable, the verb stress on the second.
normal.cn: 名词重音在第一音节，动词重音在第二音节。

normal.en: Rebel against is the phrase for refusing a person or a rule.
normal.cn: rebel against 是拒绝某人或某条规则的固定搭配。

normal.en: Rebellion and rebellious grow from the same root, one an act and one a trait.
normal.cn: rebellion 与 rebellious 同根，一个指行为，一个指性格。

abstract.en: Every rebel begins by deciding that an old order no longer deserves obedience.
abstract.cn: 每个反叛者都从判定旧秩序不再值得服从开始。

abstract.en: Rebellion is renewal with a cost, a war fought again in a smaller room.
abstract.cn: 反叛是带代价的更新，是在更小的房间里再打一场战争。

abstract.en: To rebel against advice is to claim the right to make one's own mistakes.
abstract.cn: 抗拒建议，就是主张自己犯错的权利。

examples.en: The rebel was arrested at dawn.
examples.cn: 那名反叛者在黎明时被捕。

examples.en: The peasants rebelled against the heavy taxes.
examples.cn: 农民们反抗沉重的赋税。

examples.en: Teenagers often rebel against their parents' advice.
examples.cn: 青少年常常抗拒父母的建议。

dict_mnemonic.text: re（再）加 bellum（战争）：再开一战的人就是 rebel——反叛者；动词就是反抗。

root: 拉丁 bellum（战争）→ 前缀 re-（再次）→ 拉丁 rebellis（重新开战者）→ 古法语 rebelle → 英语 rebel；同族有 rebellion、rebellious。

sensesIntro.en: The core is renewed war; the senses cover the person, the act, and the everyday refusal of rules.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「重新开战」；义项覆盖人、行为，以及日常对规则的抗拒。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a crowd holding torches, standing with its back to a throne.
core.cn: 核心意象：人群举着火把，背对王座站成一排。

branches.en: a figure with a raised torch
branches.cn: 高举火把的身影

branches.en: a village rising in arms
branches.cn: 拿起武器的村庄

branches.en: a teenager turning away from advice
branches.cn: 扭头不听建议的少年

branches.en: the person and the uprising
branches.cn: 人与起义

branches.cn: 公开的战争与私人的拒绝

intro.en: The word joins a Latin prefix to the Latin word for war, then passes through French into English.
intro.cn: 这个词把拉丁前缀与拉丁语的「战争」结合，再经法语进入英语。

latinIntro.en: Its Latin base is bellum, war, with the prefix re- meaning again.
latinIntro.cn: 其拉丁词根是 bellum（战争），前缀 re- 意为「再次」。

definition_zh: 在情感上；感情上；激动地
definition_en: in a way connected with emotions; with strong feeling; in terms of emotional needs
core_image: 一条看不见的线直接连到心口，轻轻一碰就起波纹
scene: 她努力把话说得平静，声音却还是变了。 She spoke emotionally about the loss.
sceneCN: 这里 emotionally 是「动情地、带着情绪地」（第 02 个义项：以强烈情感的方式）；句意是她谈到失去时动了情。

pos.zh: 副词：在情感上；感情上；激动地

derivatives.zh: 去掉 -ly 得到形容词，义为「情感的」
核心名词，义为「情感；情绪」
同词族形容词，义为「引起强烈情感的」

senses.title: In terms of emotions
senses.definition: in a way that concerns a person's feelings or emotional needs
senses.definitionCN: 在涉及一个人的感受或情感需求的方面
senses.example: The children were emotionally neglected.
senses.exampleCN: 这些孩子在情感上被忽视了。
senses.why: The adverb adds -ly to emotional, so it marks the emotional dimension of a situation rather than its physical side.
senses.whyCN: 这个副词由 emotional 加 -ly 构成，所以它标记的是一件事的情感维度，而不是物理层面。

senses.title: With strong feeling
senses.definition: in a manner showing strong or barely controlled feeling
senses.definitionCN: 以表现出强烈或难以控制的感情的方式
senses.example: She spoke emotionally about the loss.
senses.exampleCN: 她谈到失去时动了情。
senses.why: When the inner pond is stirred, speech itself can shake, so the adverb describes an action carried out with visible feeling.
senses.whyCN: 内心的水面被搅动时，连说话都会发抖，所以这个副词形容一个带着明显感情完成的动作。

senses.title: In an easily affected state
senses.definition: in a state where feelings are easily aroused or hard to manage
senses.definitionCN: 处于感情容易被激起或难以控制的状态
senses.example: He reacted emotionally to the criticism.
senses.exampleCN: 他对批评的反应很情绪化。
senses.why: A person whose feelings rise quickly acts from that rising rather than from calm thought, so the adverb can also signal a low emotional threshold.
senses.whyCN: 感受升得快的人会顺着这股上升行动，而不是按冷静思考行动，所以这个副词也能暗示情感门槛很低。

intro.en: Emotionally is emotional plus -ly, a regular English adverb built on the Latin root for moving and stirring.
intro.cn: emotionally 是 emotional 加 -ly 构成的规则副词，其根仍是表示移动与搅动的拉丁词。

items.en: The verb meant to move out or stir up.
items.cn: 这个动词意为移出、激起。

items.en: The noun named a stirring of the mind.
items.cn: 名词指心绪被搅动。

items.en: The adjective appeared with the ending -al.
items.cn: 形容词以 -al 词尾出现。

items.en: English added -ly to make the adverb emotionally.
items.cn: 英语再加 -ly，构成副词 emotionally。

items.en: The adverb now covers emotional needs, visible feeling and emotional reactions.
items.cn: 现代英语中，这个副词涵盖情感需求、外露感情与情绪化反应。

note.en: The look-alike group follows the emotion family; the near-meaning group separates sentimental, passionate and warm manners.
note.cn: 形近组沿着 emotion 词族展开；近义组区分感伤、激情与温暖的方式。

entries.definition: Relating to or showing emotion.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「情感的、情绪化的」，是本词的基础。

entries.definition: A strong feeling.
Arousing strong feeling.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「引起强烈情感的」。

entries.definition: In an overly tender or nostalgic way.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「感伤地、多愁善感地」。

entries.definition: With very strong feeling or belief.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「充满激情地」，强度更高。

entries.definition: In a friendly and affectionate way.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「热情地、亲切地」，情感色彩更温和。

normalIntro.en: These hooks start from emotional plus -ly, then point the adverb at needs, at speech and at reactions.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子从 emotional 加 -ly 出发，再让这个副词分别指向需求、言语与反应。

normal.en: Emotional plus -ly makes the adverb.
normal.cn: emotional 加 -ly 构成副词。

normal.en: Emotionally exhausted means tired in the heart.
normal.cn: emotionally exhausted 就是心也累了。

normal.en: To speak emotionally is to let the voice shake.
normal.cn: speak emotionally 就是让声音发抖。

normal.en: An emotionally charged room is full of feeling.
normal.cn: emotionally charged 的房间充满情绪。

normal.en: Emotionally unavailable means the door to feeling is shut.
normal.cn: emotionally unavailable 指通往感受的门关着。

abstract.en: Picture a thread running from the words straight to the heart.
abstract.cn: 想象一根线从话语直接连到心口。

abstract.en: The adverb tells you which layer of life is being touched.
abstract.cn: 这个副词告诉你被碰到的是生活的哪一层。

abstract.en: Emotionally is a spotlight aimed at the inner weather.
abstract.cn: emotionally 就是一束照向内心天气的聚光灯。

examples.en: The children were emotionally neglected.
examples.cn: 这些孩子在情感上被忽视了。

examples.en: She spoke emotionally about the loss.
examples.cn: 她谈到失去时动了情。

examples.en: He reacted emotionally to the criticism.
examples.cn: 他对批评的反应很情绪化。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「一摸身脑里」——心口被摸到，话就从情绪里出来

root: 由 emotional 加副词词尾 -ly 构成；emotion 经法语来自拉丁语 emovere，即 e-（向外）加 movere（移动、搅动）。

sensesIntro.en: Emotionally marks the emotional side of a situation, an act done with visible feeling, and a state easily stirred.
sensesIntro.cn: emotionally 标记一件事的情感层面、一个带着明显感情的动作，以及容易被搅动的状态。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a thread from the words straight to the heart.
core.cn: 核心意象：一根线从话语直连到心口。

branches.en: THE DIMENSION: needs and neglect on the feeling side.
branches.cn: 维度线：感受层面的需求与忽视。

branches.en: THE MANNER: an action carried out with feeling.
branches.cn: 方式线：带着感情完成的动作。

branches.en: THE REACTION: feelings rising before thought.
branches.cn: 反应线：感情先于思考升起。

branches.en: FIELD AND STYLE: the emotional domain and an emotional manner.
branches.cn: 领域与方式：情感领域与动情方式。

branches.en: EXPRESSION AND TEMPER: what is shown and what is easily stirred.
branches.cn: 表达与性情：表现出来的与容易被激起的。

intro.en: Emotionally is emotional plus -ly, the regular English ending for manner adverbs.
intro.cn: emotionally 是 emotional 加 -ly，这是英语构成方式副词的标准词尾。

latinIntro.en: The root movere is Latin, while -al and -ly came into English through French and Germanic habits.
latinIntro.cn: 词根 movere 是拉丁语，-al 与 -ly 则分别经法语与日耳曼语习惯进入英语。

items.example: It is the noun behind the adjective.
items.exampleCN: 它是形容词背后的名词。
它出现在 emotion 里面。

definition_zh: 第八十；八十分之一；八十岁生日
definition_en: the eightieth in order, one of eighty equal parts, or the eightieth birthday of someone
core_image: 桌上插满细蜡烛，蛋糕几乎被烛光盖住
scene: 全村人挤进小屋，为老人过第八十个生日。 The whole village came to her eightieth birthday.
sceneCN: 这里 eightieth 是「第八十个」（第 1 个义项：排在另外七十九个之后的位置）；句意是全村人来给她过第八十个生日。

pos.zh: 数词（序数）：第八十；八十分之一
名词：第八十个；八十分之一；（口语）八十岁生日

derivatives.zh: 由本词去掉序数词尾 -eth 并还原 y 得到，义为「八十」
与本词同出 eight 词族，义为「八」，是 eighty 的词基
由本词加副词后缀 -ly 构成，义为「第八十点」

senses.title: The eightieth in order
senses.definition: coming after seventy-nine others in a series
senses.definitionCN: 在一串中排在另外七十九个之后
senses.example: The eightieth page is missing from this copy.
senses.exampleCN: 这一本缺了第八十页。
senses.why: Eightieth is eighty plus the ordinal -eth, with y changed to ie; it marks the place after seventy-nine others.
senses.whyCN: eightieth 是 eighty 加序数词尾 -eth、y 变 ie 而成，标记的是排在七十九个之后的位置。

senses.title: One of eighty equal parts
senses.definition: one of eighty equal parts of a whole
senses.definitionCN: 一个整体被均分为八十份时的一份
senses.example: An eightieth of the profit goes to the fund.
senses.exampleCN: 利润的八十分之一进入基金。
senses.why: Cut a whole into eighty and each piece is an eightieth, the ordinal used as a fraction.
senses.whyCN: 把一个整体切成八十份，每一份就是一个 eightieth，序数词被当作分数使用。

senses.title: An eightieth birthday
senses.definition: the birthday on which someone turns eighty, or the celebration of it
senses.definitionCN: 某人满八十岁那天的生日，或为此举行的庆祝
senses.example: The whole village came to her eightieth birthday.
senses.exampleCN: 全村人都来给她过八十岁生日。
senses.why: Counting years in order reaches the eightieth, so the ordinal stands alone as the name of that birthday.
senses.whyCN: 按顺序数年份会数到第八十个，于是这个序数词单独成词，成了那个生日的名字。

intro.en: Eightieth is Old English eahtatiggoða, the ordinal of eahtatig, eighty, which was itself eight groups of ten.
intro.cn: eightieth 是古英语 eahtatiggoða，即 eahtatig（八十）的序数形式，而八十本身就是八个十。

items.en: Eahta meant eight and begins the whole family.
items.cn: eahta 意为「八」，是整个词族的起点。

items.en: The element tig meant a group of ten, so eahtatig was eight tens.
items.cn: 成分 tig 意为「一组十」，所以 eahtatig 就是八个十。

items.en: The compound named eighty, the count built on eight.
items.cn: 这个复合词指八十，是建立在「八」上的计数。

items.en: The ordinal added the -tha ending to mark the eightieth place.
items.cn: 序数形式加上 -tha 词尾，标记第八十的位置。

items.en: Middle English reshaped the ending to -ethe and later -ieth.
items.cn: 中古英语把词尾改写为 -ethe，后来又变成 -ieth。

items.en: The modern form is eighty plus -eth, with y written as ie.
items.cn: 现代词形是 eighty 加 -eth，其中 y 写作 ie。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the numerals built on eight; the near-meaning group gathers words for late old age and for a hundredth part.
note.cn: 形近组收由 eight 构成的数词；近义组收表示高龄与百分之一的词。

entries.definition: The number 80, eight tens.
entries.definitionCN: 数词，义为「八十」，即八个十，是本词的词基。

entries.definition: The number 18, built as eight plus ten rather than eight tens.
entries.definitionCN: 数词，义为「十八」，是八加十而不是八个十。

entries.definition: The ordinal of eight, built with the same -th family of endings.
entries.definitionCN: 序数词，义为「第八」，用同一类词尾构成。

entries.definition: The ordinal of a hundred, or one of a hundred equal parts.
entries.definitionCN: 序数词，义为「第一百」或「百分之一」，与本词结构相同。

entries.definition: A person who is between eighty and eighty-nine years old.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「八十多岁的人」，与本词的生日义相关。

entries.definition: A special anniversary, often a fiftieth or a significant round number.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「纪念大庆」，常指五十周年等重要整数周年。

normalIntro.en: These hooks build the word from eight tens, then bend the tail into an ordinal and a fraction.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子从八个十出发，再把词尾弯成序数词与分数。

normal.en: Eighty is eight tens; eightieth is the place that count reaches.
normal.cn: eighty 是八个十；eightieth 是这个计数走到的那一位。

normal.en: The y turns into ie before -eth: eighty, eightieth.
normal.cn: y 在 -eth 前变成 ie：eighty、eightieth。

normal.en: One eightieth is a very thin slice of a whole.
normal.cn: 八十分之一是从整体上切下的极薄一片。

normal.en: Candles crowd the cake: that is an eightieth birthday.
normal.cn: 蜡烛挤满蛋糕：那就是第八十个生日。

normal.en: It follows eighteenth in the same pattern, one tier higher.
normal.cn: 它沿着 eighteenth 的同一套模式，只是再高一档。

abstract.en: Picture a cake almost hidden under eighty thin candles.
abstract.cn: 想象一块几乎被八十根细蜡烛盖住的蛋糕。

abstract.en: The same form can be a position, a fraction, or a life milestone.
abstract.cn: 同一个形式可以是位置、分数，或人生里程碑。

abstract.en: Eightieth is eight tens counted out one by one.
abstract.cn: eightieth 就是把八个十一个一个数出来。

examples.en: The eightieth page is missing from this copy.
examples.cn: 这一本缺了第八十页。

examples.en: An eightieth of the profit goes to the fund.
examples.cn: 利润的八十分之一进入基金。

examples.en: The whole village came to her eightieth birthday.
examples.cn: 全村人都来给她过八十岁生日。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「诶提厄思」——蛋糕上插满八十根细蜡烛

root: 古英语 eahtatig 由 eahta「八」与 tig「一组十」复合为「八十」，其序数形式 eahtatiggoða 即「第八十」；现代词为 eighty 加 -eth。

sensesIntro.en: Three senses of eightieth: the eightieth position, one of eighty equal parts, and an eightieth birthday.
sensesIntro.cn: eightieth 的三个义项：排在第八十位、八十分之一，以及八十岁生日。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a cake almost hidden under eighty thin candles.
core.cn: 核心意象：一块几乎被八十根细蜡烛盖住的蛋糕。

branches.en: THE QUEUE: it stands after seventy-nine others.
branches.cn: 队伍线：它排在另外七十九个之后。

branches.en: THE SLICE: one of eighty equal parts.
branches.cn: 切片线：八十等份中的一份。

branches.en: THE CANDLES: the birthday on which someone turns eighty.
branches.cn: 蜡烛线：某人满八十岁那天的生日。

branches.en: THE ORDER: one ordinal both counts position and divides a whole.
branches.cn: 顺序线：同一个序数词既数位置，也切分整体。

branches.en: THE YEARS: a birthday is simply the eightieth item in a count of years.
branches.cn: 年岁线：生日不过是年数计到第八十项。

intro.en: Eightieth is a Germanic numeral with the ordinal ending -eth; there is no Latin layer in the word.

latinIntro.en: The numeral family is Germanic, so no Latin entry is claimed; only the Indo-European root for eight is reconstructed.

definition_zh: 悲剧；惨案；不幸事件；悲剧体裁
definition_en: a very sad event or situation, or a serious play that ends unhappily
core_image: 空荡的舞台上，一只倒下的面具
scene: 最后一幕落下时，主角已经倒在台上，观众席里没有人马上起身鼓掌。 The play is a tragedy; everyone on stage loses something by the end.
sceneCN: 这里 tragedy 是「悲剧」（第 1 个义项：结局悲惨的严肃戏剧）；句意说这是一出悲剧，到结尾台上每个人都失去了些什么。

derivatives.zh: 由同一词干加 -ic 构成，义为「悲剧的；悲惨的」
由形容词加 -ally 构成，义为「悲惨地」
由同一词干加 -ian 构成，义为「悲剧演员；悲剧作家」

senses.title: A serious play with an unhappy end
senses.definition: a serious drama in which the main character suffers greatly and usually dies
senses.definitionCN: 主角遭受重大苦难、通常以死亡收场的严肃戏剧
senses.example: We studied three tragedies by Shakespeare this term.
senses.exampleCN: 这学期我们学了三部莎士比亚的悲剧。
senses.why: The Greek word names a specific kind of drama, and the literary sense remains the centre of the word.
senses.whyCN: 希腊文原名就指某一类戏剧，文学义至今仍是这个词的核心。

senses.title: A very sad event
senses.definition: a terrible event that causes great suffering, such as an accident or a disaster
senses.definitionCN: 造成巨大痛苦的可怕事件，如事故或灾难
senses.example: The fire was a tragedy that the village has never forgotten.
senses.exampleCN: 那场大火是这个村子从未忘掉的惨剧。
senses.why: Real disasters were said to have the shape of a stage tragedy, and the word passed into ordinary life.
senses.whyCN: 现实的灾难被说成具有舞台悲剧的形态，于是这个词进入了日常生活。

senses.title: Great suffering that seems fated
senses.definition: a pattern of suffering that appears inevitable and beyond human control
senses.definitionCN: 看起来无可避免、超出人力控制的一连串苦难
senses.example: The family's story has the slow tragedy of a Greek play.
senses.exampleCN: 这家人的经历有希腊剧那样缓慢的悲剧性。
senses.why: In Greek drama the hero's fall is fated, and that sense of inevitability colours the everyday word.
senses.whyCN: 希腊剧中英雄的坠落是命定的，这种必然感为日常用法染了色。

senses.title: The genre of such plays
senses.definition: the whole class of dramatic works of this kind, often opposed to comedy
senses.definitionCN: 这一类戏剧作品的总称，常与喜剧相对
senses.example: The two masks of the theatre stand for tragedy and comedy.
senses.exampleCN: 剧场的两副面具代表悲剧与喜剧。
senses.why: As a genre, tragedy is a form rather than an event, and criticism keeps the word in this technical sense.
senses.whyCN: 作为体裁，tragedy 是一种形式而非事件，文艺批评一直保持着这个术语义。

senses.title: A regrettable situation
senses.definition: used in the pattern it is a tragedy that to say something is deeply regrettable
senses.definitionCN: 用于 it is a tragedy that 句型，表示某事令人深感痛心
senses.example: It is a tragedy that so many old trees were cut down.
senses.exampleCN: 这么多老树被砍掉，实在令人痛心。
senses.why: The word's weight becomes a way of expressing strong regret, even over things that cost no lives.
senses.whyCN: 这个词的分量成了一种表达强烈遗憾的方式，即使并不涉及生命。

intro.en: Tragedy comes from Greek tragoidia, literally goat-song, from tragos, goat, and aeidein, to sing, probably from the goat given as a prize.
intro.cn: tragedy 来自希腊语 tragoidia，字面是「山羊之歌」，由 tragos（山羊）与 aeidein（歌唱）构成，可能源自律唱比赛的羊奖品。

items.en: Tragoidia is the name of a choral performance in Athens, built from tragos, goat, and ode, song.
items.cn: tragoidia 是雅典一种合唱歌舞的名称，由 tragos（山羊）与 ode（歌）构成。

items.en: The goat may have been the prize for the best chorus, or the animal sacrificed before the performance.
items.cn: 山羊可能是最佳合唱队的奖品，也可能是演出前献祭的牺牲。

items.en: In Athens tragedy becomes the great serious drama of Aeschylus, Sophocles, and Euripides.
items.cn: 在雅典，tragedy 成为埃斯库罗斯、索福克勒斯与欧里庇得斯的伟大严肃戏剧。

items.en: Latin tragoedia borrows the Greek word and passes the dramatic sense to European schools.
items.cn: 拉丁语 tragoedia 借走这个希腊词，并把戏剧含义传给欧洲的学校。

items.en: Middle English tragedy first means a story, often in verse, with a sad ending.
items.cn: 中古英语 tragedy 最初指一个以悲收场的故事，常为韵文。

items.en: From the eighteenth century the word also describes real disasters, and the figurative use widens from there.
items.cn: 十八世纪起，这个词也用来描述真实的灾难，比喻用法自此扩展。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words from the same Greek stage family, while the near-meaning group gathers words for disaster and suffering.
note.cn: 形近组收集同一希腊舞台词族的词，近义组收集表示灾难与苦难的词。

in a very sad way
a funny play or film with a happy end
the movement of vehicles
entries.definitionCN: 交通，拼写相近而来源不同

entries.definition: a sudden event that causes great harm
a very great disaster

normalIntro.en: These memories work from the goat-song origin, from the theatre masks, and from the pattern it is a tragedy that.
normalIntro.cn: 下面几条从「山羊之歌」的来源、剧场面具以及 it is a tragedy that 句型入手。

normal.en: Tragos plus ode: goat song. The strange name survives inside the serious play.
normal.cn: tragos 加 ode，就是山羊之歌。这个古怪的名字藏在严肃戏剧里面。

normal.en: Two masks: the smiling one is comedy, the weeping one is tragedy.
normal.cn: 两副面具：笑的那副是喜剧，哭的那副是悲剧。

normal.en: Tragedy as a genre ends badly; tragedy as an event hurts now.
normal.cn: 作为体裁的悲剧结局不好；作为事件的悲剧当下就伤人。

normal.en: It is a tragedy that plus a fact is a formal way of saying something is deeply sad.
normal.cn: it is a tragedy that 加一个事实，是表达「令人深感痛心」的正规说法。

normal.en: The -dy ending is not a suffix, so remove nothing: the whole word is the root.
normal.cn: 词尾 -dy 不是后缀，不要拆掉，整个词就是词根。

abstract.en: Picture a single actor alone on a lit stage after everyone else has left.
abstract.cn: 想象灯还亮着，别人都走了，台上只剩一个演员。

abstract.en: Think of a goat standing quietly at the back of a Greek chorus, waiting to be a prize.
abstract.cn: 想一只山羊安静地站在希腊合唱队后面，等着当奖品。

abstract.en: A tragedy is a loss that could not have been stopped in time.
abstract.cn: 悲剧是一场来不及被拦住的失去。

examples.en: The accident on the bridge was a terrible tragedy.
examples.cn: 桥上的那场事故是可怕的惨剧。

examples.en: He wrote three tragedies before he was thirty.
examples.cn: 他三十岁前写了三部悲剧。

examples.en: It is a tragedy that she left the course so early.
examples.cn: 她这么早就离开课程，实在可惜。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「踹几只」——舞台上踹倒了那几只面具，悲剧开场。

root: 希腊语 tragoidia（山羊之歌）= tragos（山羊）+ ode（歌）→ 拉丁语 tragoedia → 中古英语 tragedy。同族词有 tragic、tragically、tragedian。

sensesIntro.en: The entry starts with the stage play, moves to real disasters that move like a play, then to the sense of fated suffering, then back to the genre in criticism, and ends with the phrase of deep regret.
sensesIntro.cn: 本词从舞台剧开始，转到像戏一样展开的现实灾难，再指命定的苦难，又回到文艺批评中的体裁义，最后落在表达深切遗憾的句型上。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a stage emptied by a story that ends in loss.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个以失去收场的故事所留下的空舞台。

branches.en: The play itself.
branches.cn: 戏剧本身。

branches.en: The real event with that shape.
branches.cn: 具有这种形态的真实事件。

branches.en: The sense that the pain was unavoidable.
branches.cn: 那种痛苦无可避免的感觉。

branches.en: The genre name in criticism.
branches.cn: 批评中的体裁名称。

branches.en: The phrase for sharp regret.
branches.cn: 表达强烈遗憾的句型。

intro.en: The word is a Greek compound whose parts are no longer felt as separate; English builds its family with -ic, -ally, and -ian.
intro.cn: 本词是希腊语复合词，各部件在英语中已不再被感知为独立成分；英语用 -ic、-ally、-ian 构成词族。

latinIntro.en: The Greek parts below are the compound's original pieces, carried into Latin as tragoedia.
latinIntro.cn: 下面列出这个希腊复合词的原始部件，它们以 tragoedia 的形式进入拉丁语。

items.example: Tragos is the first half of the compound.
Ode is the second half of the compound.
A tragedian is an actor or writer of tragedy.
items.exampleCN: tragedian 是悲剧演员或作家。

items.example: The ending comes from the Latinized form.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾来自拉丁化形式。

items.example: The goat is the picture under the word.
items.exampleCN: 山羊是这个词底下的画面。

items.example: The chorus sang the song that named the genre.
items.exampleCN: 合唱队唱的歌给这一体裁命名。

definition_zh: 内部；里面；adj. 内部的；内地的
definition_en: the inside part of something, or relating to the inside
core_image: 从窗外看进去，屋里亮着灯，家具的轮廓清清楚楚
scene: 车停在路边，雨刷还在动，车内仪表盘泛着微光。 The interior of the old church is darker than the square outside.
sceneCN: 这里 interior 是「内部、里面」（第 1 个义项：某物的内侧空间），句意这座老教堂内部比外面广场更暗。画面里的物件：车内仪表盘、教堂穹顶、窗外的光。

pos.zh: 名词：内部；里面；内地；内政

derivatives.zh: 由本词加 -ize 构成，义为「内化」
由本词加 -ly 构成，义为「在内部」
由同一词干构成，义为「内部的」
由相反方向的前缀构成，义为「外部」

senses.title: The inside space
senses.definition: the inside part of a building, room, or vehicle
senses.definitionCN: 建筑、房间或车辆内部的那部分
senses.example: The interior of the van smelled of new paint.
senses.exampleCN: 货车内部有一股新油漆味。
senses.why: Latin interior is the comparative of the adjective meaning "inner".
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 interior 是意为「内部的」形容词的比较级。

senses.title: The land far from the coast
senses.definition: the central part of a country, away from the sea and borders
senses.definitionCN: 一国的中心部分，远离海岸与边境
senses.example: Traders carried salt far into the interior.
senses.exampleCN: 商人们运盐深入内陆。
senses.why: Explorers spoke of the interior because maps stopped at the coast.
senses.whyCN: 航海者谈「内陆」，因为地图止于海岸线。

senses.title: The inside story
senses.definition: the part of a person or a thing that is not shown outwardly
senses.definitionCN: 人或事物不外露的那部分
senses.example: Her calm voice hid a troubled interior.
senses.exampleCN: 她平静的声音下藏着不安的内心。
senses.why: The spatial word moves inward to name hidden feeling.
senses.whyCN: 这个空间词向内延伸，用来指隐藏的感受。

senses.title: Home affairs
senses.definition: the domestic affairs of a country as opposed to its foreign policy
senses.definitionCN: 一国的国内事务，与外交政策相对
senses.example: The interior minister promised tighter border checks.
senses.exampleCN: 内政部长承诺加强边境检查。
senses.why: Governments name domestic affairs by the word for inside space.
senses.whyCN: 政府用表示内部空间的词来命名国内事务。

intro.en: Interior is the Latin comparative of an inner adjective; it came to English as both noun and adjective.
intro.cn: interior 是拉丁语中表示「内部的」形容词的比较级，作为名词与形容词一同进入英语。

items.en: The preposition inter "among" gave rise to an adjective for what lies inside.
items.cn: 介词 inter「在……之中」生出一个指「在里面」的形容词。

items.en: Interior was its comparative, meaning more inside, as in "interior pars".
items.cn: interior 是它的比较级，意为「更靠里的」，如 interior pars。

items.en: Writers used interior for the inner area of a land or a house.
items.cn: 作家用 interior 指土地或房舍的里侧区域。

items.en: English borrowed it in the sixteenth century as an adjective.
items.cn: 英语在十六世纪先把它作形容词借入。

items.en: The noun spread to mean innermost land, inner rooms, and finally private feeling.
items.cn: 名词随后扩展到「内陆」「内室」，乃至私人的内心。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the inner root; the near-meaning group holds other words for the inside.
note.cn: 形近组共享「内部」词根；近义组收其他表示内部的词。

entries.definition: Inside an organisation or a body.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「内部的」，指组织或身体之内。

entries.definition: The outside surface, the exact opposite.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「外部」，正好相反。

entries.definition: In the inner part; rare but real.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「在内部」，少见但真实。

entries.definition: The everyday word for what is within.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「里面」，最日常的说法。

entries.definition: The country's middle, away from the coast.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词或名词，义为「内陆的」。

entries.definition: Of the home, or of affairs inside a country.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「家庭的；国内的」。

normalIntro.en: The hooks use the comparison hidden in interior and the places it is used.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子利用 interior 中藏着的比较意味，并挂上它常用的场合。

normal.en: Interior is the more inside one, the comparative of inner.
normal.cn: interior 是「更靠里的那个」，即「内部」的比较级。

normal.en: Interior design works on the inside of rooms.
normal.cn: 室内设计做的是房间的内侧。

normal.en: Explorers carried salt into the interior.
normal.cn: 探险者把盐运进内陆。

normal.en: The interior ministry handles borders and police.
normal.cn: 内政部管边境与警察。

normal.en: A calm face can hide an uncertain interior.
normal.cn: 平静的面容可以掩盖不确定的内心。

abstract.en: The word turns a country into a house with a middle.
abstract.cn: 这个词把一个国家变成有里屋的房子。

abstract.en: Interior is a compass pointing inward.
abstract.cn: interior 是一只指向内侧的罗盘。

abstract.en: Some journeys into the interior never cross a border.
abstract.cn: 有些走向内陆的旅程从不过境。

examples.en: The interior of the theatre was painted deep red.
examples.cn: 剧院内部漆成了深红色。

examples.en: Rain rarely reaches the dry interior of the island.
examples.cn: 雨水很少落到岛上干旱的内陆。

examples.en: He spoke calmly, but his interior was in turmoil.
examples.cn: 他语气平静，内心却一片混乱。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「因特瑞尔」——网上的内容都在里面，所以是内部

root: 拉丁语 inter「在……之中」→ 形容词 inner 族 → 比较级 interior「更靠里的」→ 英语 interior。反义：exterior。

sensesIntro.en: Four senses: inner space, inland regions, hidden feeling, and home affairs.
sensesIntro.cn: 四个义项：内部空间、内陆地区、隐藏的感受，以及国内政务。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a lit room seen through a window at night.
core.cn: 核心意象：夜里透过窗户看见一间亮着灯的房间。

branches.en: THE VAN: the inside is a separate space from the street.
branches.cn: 货车这条线：内部是与街道分开的一处空间。

branches.en: THE SALT TRADERS: the map continues past the coast.
branches.cn: 盐商这条线：地图越过海岸继续延伸。

branches.en: THE CALM VOICE: the inward room of a person.
branches.cn: 平静声音这条线：人里面的那间屋子。

branches.en: THE MINISTRY: a nation is imagined as a house.
branches.cn: 内阁这条线：国家被想象成一座房子。

branches.en: THE LINK: politics borrows the house metaphor.
branches.cn: 连接线：政治借用了房子的比喻。

intro.en: Interior = inter- "among" + the comparative ending -ior, literally "more within".
intro.cn: interior = inter-「在……之中」+ 比较级词尾 -ior，字面即「更在里面的」。

latinIntro.en: Latin interior is attested as both adjective and noun; the ending -ior is the Latin comparative.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 interior 作形容词与名词均有记载，-ior 是拉丁比较级词尾。

items.exampleCN: 它把「在里面」变成「更在里面」。

items.example: A near twin with a different ending.
items.exampleCN: 另一个同源近亲，词尾不同。

definition_zh: 可比较的；类似的；相当
definition_en: similar enough to be compared with something else, or good enough to be equal to it
core_image: 两把并排放在桌上的尺子，长度几乎一样
scene: 同事把两份方案的报价摊在桌上逐项对照。 The two plans are comparable in cost but not in speed.
sceneCN: 这里 comparable 指「可比较的；相当的」（第 1 个义项：能够放在一起比较）；句意是两份方案在成本上相当，在速度上却不同。

pos.zh: 可比较的；类似的；相当的

senses.title: Able to be compared
senses.definition: similar enough in size, value or quality to be compared
senses.definitionCN: 在大小、价值或质量上相似到可以相互比较
senses.example: The two cities are comparable in size.
senses.exampleCN: 这两座城市规模相当。
senses.why: Comparison only works when the two sides stand on common ground.
senses.whyCN: 比较只有在双方有共同基准时才成立。

senses.title: Good enough to match
senses.definition: as good as another thing of the same kind
senses.definitionCN: 与同类事物一样好
senses.example: Her salary is comparable to that of a senior engineer.
senses.exampleCN: 她的薪水相当于一名高级工程师。
senses.why: From being measurable, the word moves to being equal in worth.
senses.whyCN: 从「可以量」进一步引申为「价值相当」。

intro.en: Comparable comes from Latin comparare, to pair things as equals, built on par, equal.
intro.cn: comparable 来自拉丁语 comparare，意为把事物作为同等者放在一起，词基 par 表示相等。

items.en: Par meant equal, level, of the same rank.
items.cn: par 表示相等、齐平、同级。

items.en: Comparare meant to set two things side by side as equals.
items.cn: comparare 意为把两样东西作为同等者并排放置。

items.en: Old French comparer kept the pairing sense.
items.cn: 古法语 comparer 保留了配对比较的意思。

items.en: English comparable first described things of equal measure.
items.cn: 英语 comparable 最初描述分量相等的事物。

items.en: It now covers costs, data and any fair comparison.
items.cn: 如今它覆盖成本、数据以及任何公平的比较。

note.en: The look-alike group holds words built on the same comparing root, and the meaning group names other ways of saying that two things are close.
note.cn: 形近组收的是建立在同一比较词根上的词，近义组列出其他表示两者相近的说法。

entries.definition: based on a comparison between things
to examine two things side by side
in a similar way
almost the same but not identical
equal in value or meaning
having the same colour or design

normalIntro.en: These hooks begin with a shared measure, then move to fair comparison and to value that stands level.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子从共同的尺度开始，再走到公平比较与不分高下的价值。

normal.en: Com- is together and par is equal, so comparable means able to stand level.
normal.cn: com- 是一起，par 是相等，comparable 就是能并肩站平。

normal.en: Two things must share a measure before they are comparable.
normal.cn: 两样东西先有共同尺度，才谈得上可比。

normal.en: Compare is the verb, comparison the noun, comparable the adjective.
normal.cn: compare 是动词，comparison 是名词，comparable 是形容词。

normal.en: In- turns it around: incomparable means beyond any rival.
normal.cn: 加上 in- 就反过来：incomparable 指无可比拟。

normal.en: A comparable salary is not the same salary, only a fair one.
normal.cn: 相当的薪水不是同一份薪水，而是公平的那一档。

abstract.en: Picture two rulers laid side by side on a desk.
abstract.cn: 想象两把尺子并排放在桌上。

abstract.en: Picture two runners crossing the line almost together.

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 comparable 记成 com（一起）加 par（相等）加 able（能）：能放在一起比而站得平，就是可比。

root: 源自拉丁语 comparare（并列比较），词基 par 表示相等，本义是能作为同等者并排放置，后引申为类似的、相当的。

sensesIntro.en: From being fit to compare, to being equal in worth.
sensesIntro.cn: 从适合拿来比较，到价值上相当。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two rulers of almost the same length lying side by side.

branches.en: Being measurable is what makes two things comparable.
branches.cn: 可被同一尺度衡量，才使两物可比。

branches.en: Value, not only size, can also be comparable.

branches.en: Both senses need a common measure, one of size and one of worth.

branches.en: Comparable stays fair: it never claims the two are identical.

intro.en: Comparable joins the Latin root par, equal, with the ending -able, able to be.

latinIntro.en: Comparare gave English a whole family: compare, comparison, comparative and comparable.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 comparare 给英语带来一整族词：compare、comparison、comparative 与 comparable。

definition_zh: 顾问；会诊医生
definition_en: an expert who gives professional advice, or a senior doctor in a hospital
core_image: 一位夹着文件夹的人，在会议桌边为客户圈出重点
scene: 医院里，主治医生请来一位专科同行一起看片子。 The consultant reviewed the scan before the operation.
sceneCN: 这里 consultant 指「会诊医生」（第 2 个义项：医院里的高级专科医生）；句意是这位会诊医生在手术前看了片子。

pos.zh: 顾问；会诊医生；专科医生

senses.title: A paid expert
senses.definition: a person paid to give expert advice in a field
senses.definitionCN: 受雇在某一领域提供专业意见的人

senses.why: Experience becomes useful to others when it is lent out.

senses.title: A senior doctor

senses.example: The consultant explained the scan results.
senses.exampleCN: 这位专科医生解释了片子结果。
senses.why: In a hospital, the one who is consulted is the one who knows most.
senses.whyCN: 在医院里，被请教的人就是懂得最多的人。

intro.en: Consultant comes from the Latin verb consultare, to take counsel, plus the person ending -ant.
intro.cn: consultant 来自拉丁语动词 consultare（商议），加上表示人的词尾 -ant。

items.en: Consulere meant to gather people and deliberate.
items.cn: consulere 意为聚集众人商议。

items.en: Consultare named the repeated asking of counsel.
items.cn: consultare 指反复征询意见。

items.en: The ending -ant marked the person doing the act.
items.cn: 词尾 -ant 标记执行该行为的人。

items.en: English consultant first meant a person asked for advice.
items.cn: 英语 consultant 最初指被请教的人。

items.en: The word became a paid professional title.
items.cn: 这个词成为带薪的职业头衔。

items.en: British hospitals use it for a senior specialist.
items.cn: 英国医院用它指高级专科医生。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the consult- family, and the meaning group names other people who supply expert knowledge.
note.cn: 形近组共享 consult- 词族，近义组列出其他提供专业知识的角色。

entries.definition: a firm that sells expert advice
a meeting to seek advice or opinion
to ask for advice or look something up
someone whose job is to give advice
a person who knows a lot about one subject
a person with great skill or knowledge

normalIntro.en: These hooks start from a folder carried into a meeting, then move to the hospital room where the senior doctor is called in.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子从被带进会议的文件夹开始，再到高级医生被请进的那间病房。

normal.en: Con- is together and sult is gather, so a consultant is the one others gather around to ask.

normal.en: A consultant is borrowed experience with a bill attached.

normal.en: In a British hospital, the consultant is the one others call.

normal.en: The title means asked, not obeyed.

normal.en: A good consultant leaves the client smarter, not dependent.

examples.en: They brought in a consultant to review the plan.

examples.en: Her father is a consultant at the city hospital.

root: 源自拉丁语 consultare（反复商议）加人称词尾 -ant，本义是被请教的人，后指收费提供专业意见的顾问与医院高级专科医生。

sensesIntro.en: From the expert a company borrows, to the senior doctor a ward calls in.
sensesIntro.cn: 从公司借来的那位专家，到病房里被请来的那位高级医生。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a person with a folder, circling the key line for a client.

branches.en: The first sense is an expert whose time is bought.

branches.en: Both senses name someone others turn to when the case is hard.

branches.en: In the ward, the title also carries the weight of a final word.
branches.cn: 在病房里，这个头衔还带着最终判断的分量。

intro.en: Consultant is consult plus the person ending -ant, from Latin consultare, to take counsel.

senses.title: A travel case

definition_zh: 脚步；脚步声；足迹；前人的道路
definition_en: the sound or act of a step, a mark left by a foot, or the path someone has taken before

senses.title: A step

senses.title: Sound of a step

senses.why: The act is heard before it is seen.

senses.why: Each step can leave a trace.

senses.title: Someone's path

senses.example: He tensed his shoulders before lifting.
senses.exampleCN: 举重前他绷紧了双肩。
senses.why: The adjective turns into an action: pulling the string on purpose.
senses.whyCN: 形容词转为动作：主动去拉那根弦。

intro.en: Tense, tight, comes from Latin tendere, to stretch, through its participle tensus. The grammar tense is a separate borrowing of Latin tempus, time.
intro.cn: 「紧绷」的 tense 源自拉丁语 tendere「拉伸」的分词 tensus；语法「时态」的 tense 则另借拉丁语 tempus「时间」。

items.en: Tendere meant to stretch; tensus meant stretched tight.
items.cn: tendere 意为拉伸；tensus 意为绷紧的。

items.en: Tendere is usually traced to a reconstructed PIE root for stretching.
items.cn: tendere 一般被追溯到重构的印欧「拉伸」词根。

items.en: Old French tens passed the tight sense into English.
items.cn: 古法语 tens 把「绷紧」义传入英语。

items.en: The grammar term entered separately from Old French temps, Latin tempus.
items.cn: 语法术语经古法语 temps（拉丁 tempus）另行进入。

items.en: Spelling merged both words as tense; context tells the time-word from the tight-word.
items.cn: 两词拼合为 tense；语境区分「时间」与「紧绷」。

note.en: Tense is compared with its stretch family and with nerves words.
note.cn: 把 tense 与「拉伸」词族及表示神经紧绷的词对比。

entries.definition: the state of being stretched or strained
the cord joining muscle and bone
a stretched cloth shelter
entries.definitionCN: 帐篷；同一拉伸词根的另一产物

entries.definition: worried and frightened about something
pulled tight, no slack
pressure or tension on body or mind

normalIntro.en: Real links: tensus stretched, the tense-tension-tendon family, and the time word hidden in grammar.
normalIntro.cn: 真实联系：tensus「绷紧」、tense/tension/tendon 词族、藏在语法里的时间词。

normal.en: Tensus means stretched: a tense rope hums when plucked.
normal.cn: tensus 意为绷紧：紧绷的绳一拨就嗡嗡响。

normal.en: Tense up before the dive: pull every string in the body.
normal.cn: 跳水前 tense up：把全身的弦都拉紧。

normal.en: Grammar tense is tempus, time wearing a verb's coat.
normal.cn: 语法 tense 就是 tempus：时间穿着动词的外衣。

normal.en: Tension in the room: everyone is a drawn bow.
normal.cn: 屋里的 tension：人人都像拉满的弓。

normal.en: A tendon is a living rope, always a little tense.
normal.cn: 肌腱是活的绳，永远微微绷着。

abstract.en: A nerve and a wire behave the same when pulled.
abstract.cn: 神经与钢丝被拉紧时表现相同。

abstract.en: Time itself is a string grammar likes to stretch.
abstract.cn: 时间本身就是一根语法爱拉紧的弦。

abstract.en: Relaxation is simply letting the string slack.
abstract.cn: 放松不过是让弦松下来。

examples.en: The room went tense when the verdict was read.
examples.cn: 宣判时屋里气氛骤然紧张。

examples.en: Past tense verbs often end in ed.
examples.cn: 过去式动词常以 ed 结尾。

examples.en: Relax your tense shoulders and breathe.
examples.cn: 放松紧绷的肩膀，深呼吸。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「摊死」——紧张得像摊开又拉死的弦，一动就断 → tense 紧张的、时态

root: 「紧绷」义：拉丁 tendere「拉伸」分词 tensus → 古法语 tens → 英语 tense；「时态」义另借拉丁 tempus「时间」（经古法语 temps），两词拼写合流。

sensesIntro.en: One spelling, two strings: the pulled cord and the stretched line of time.
sensesIntro.cn: 一个拼写，两根弦：被拉紧的绳与被拉开的时间线。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a string pulled to its limit.
core.cn: 核心意象：被拉到极限的弦。

branches.en: The literal cord, humming.
branches.cn: 字面之弦，嗡嗡作响。

branches.en: The body and the room both tighten.
branches.cn: 身体与房间都会收紧。

branches.en: Grammar keeps time on a line.
branches.cn: 语法把时间排在一条线上。

branches.en: A drawn bow is a waiting sentence.
branches.cn: 拉满的弓是一句等待中的判词。

branches.en: Release is the other half of tense.
branches.cn: 「松开」是 tense 的另一半。

intro.en: Tense shares the tendere stretch family with tension, tendon and tent.
intro.cn: tense 与 tension、tendon、tent 同属 tendere「拉伸」词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin tendere, to stretch, has the participle tensus, source of the tight sense; the grammar tense is from tempus, time.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 tendere「拉伸」分词 tensus 是「紧绷」义之源；语法义出自 tempus「时间」。

definition_zh: 多样的；不同的
definition_en: of many different kinds, or clearly different from one another
core_image: 一张长桌上摆着十几个地方的菜，颜色气味全不一样
scene: 长桌从这头摆到那头，盘子里的颜色没有一样重复。 The city has a diverse population.
sceneCN: 这里 diverse 指「多种多样的」（第 1 个义项：种类很多）；句意是这座城市的人口构成十分多样。

senses.title: Made of many kinds
senses.definition: made up of many different kinds of people or things
senses.definitionCN: 由许多不同种类的人或物组成
senses.example: The class is diverse in age and background.
senses.exampleCN: 这个班在年龄与背景上都很杂。
senses.why: A room with many voices is harder to sum up in one word.
senses.whyCN: 满是不同声音的房间，很难用一个词概括。

senses.title: Different from something else
senses.definition: clearly unlike another thing in nature or form
senses.definitionCN: 在性质或形态上与另一物明显不一样
senses.example: Their views are diverse on this point.
senses.exampleCN: 在这一点上他们的看法各不相同。
senses.why: To differ is to turn away on a road you once shared.
senses.whyCN: 所谓不同，就是在同一条路上各自转开。

intro.en: Diverse is Latin diversus, turned aside, from divertere, to turn in different directions.
intro.cn: diverse 是拉丁语 diversus（转开），来自 divertere（转向不同方向）。

items.en: Vertere meant to turn or turn around.
items.cn: vertere 指转动或转身。

items.en: Di- pulled the turning into two directions.
items.cn: 前缀 di- 把转动拉向两个方向。

items.en: Diversus described things turned away from each other.
items.cn: diversus 描述彼此转开的东西。

items.en: English used it for things unlike in kind.
items.cn: 英语借入时说种类不相同的东西。

items.en: The sense of many kinds together grew strong.
items.cn: 后来「多种并存」的意思变强。

items.en: Today a diverse team is valued for its differences.
items.cn: 今天多元的团队正因差异而受重视。

note.en: The look-alike group keeps the vertere stem, while the meaning group gathers words for many kinds.
note.cn: 形近组共享 vertere 这段词干，近义组则是几个表示种类多的词。

entries.definition: the state of having many kinds
to add more kinds to something
a turning aside, or a pleasant change
of several different kinds
more than one and not all alike
made of unlike parts put together

normalIntro.en: These hooks begin with a long table of unlike dishes and end with two views turning apart.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从一张摆满不同菜的长桌开始，落到两种各自转开的看法。

normal.en: Di- plus verse: the roads turn in different directions.
normal.cn: di 加 verse，路朝不同方向转开。

normal.en: The market sells diverse goods from a dozen regions.
normal.cn: 这个市场卖着十几个地区的各色货物。

normal.en: A diverse team argues more and misses less.
normal.cn: 多元的团队争得更多，漏掉的更少。

normal.en: Her interests are diverse: birds, boats and old maps.
normal.cn: 她的兴趣很杂：鸟、船和旧地图。

normal.en: The two accounts are diverse in almost every detail.
normal.cn: 这两种说法几乎每个细节都不同。

abstract.en: Picture one road splitting into many smaller roads.
abstract.cn: 想象一条路分成许多小路。

abstract.en: Picture a table where no two bowls hold the same thing.
abstract.cn: 想象一张桌子，没有两只碗装同样的东西。

abstract.en: Picture two people walking off in opposite directions.
abstract.cn: 想象两个人朝相反方向走开。

examples.en: The city has a diverse population.
examples.cn: 这座城市的人口构成很多元。

examples.en: Her reading is more diverse than mine.
examples.cn: 她读的东西比我的杂得多。

examples.en: The two villages are diverse in language and food.
examples.cn: 这两个村子在语言和饮食上都不一样。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 diverse 记成「各自转开」：di 表示分开，verse 表示转，路朝不同方向转开，就有了各种各样的差别。

root: 源自拉丁语 diversus，来自 divertere（转向不同方向），由 di-（分开）与 vertere（转）组成。本义是彼此转开、不朝一处，因此既指种类繁多，也指两物在性质上不同。

sensesIntro.en: From a road splitting into many to two views that no longer face the same way.
sensesIntro.cn: 从一条路分成许多条，到两种不再朝同一方向的看法。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one long table where no two dishes share a colour.
core.cn: 核心意象：一张长桌，没有两道菜颜色相同。

branches.en: The first sense is many kinds standing together.
branches.cn: 第一个义项是许多种类站在一起。

branches.en: The second sense is one thing turning away from another.
branches.cn: 第二个义项是一物与另一物转开。

branches.en: Both senses begin with a turning apart.
branches.cn: 两个义项都从转开开始。

branches.en: Both make a single label feel too small.
branches.cn: 两个义项都让一个标签显得不够用。

branches.en: Only the first sense needs a crowd of kinds.
branches.cn: 只有第一个义项需要一大群种类。

intro.en: Diverse belongs to the vertere family, where Latin vertere, to turn, gives a crowd of turning words.
intro.cn: diverse 属于 vertere 一族，拉丁语 vertere（转）生出一大串表示转的词。

latinIntro.en: Latin vertere, to turn, gives diverse and divert; di- turns the two paths away from each other.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 vertere（转）给出 diverse 与 divert，前缀 di- 把两条路彼此转开。

items.meaning: the state of having many kinds
items.example: The island is known for its diversity.

items.exampleCN: 这组人受过的训练很杂。

items.example: The road diversion added ten minutes.
They converted the barn into a house.
items.exampleCN: 他们把谷仓改成了住宅。

definition_zh: 日报；杂志；期刊；日志；日记
definition_en: a magazine or newspaper on a serious subject, or a daily written record of what happens
core_image: 一叠按日期装订起来、纸边写满小字的册子
scene: 图书馆的报刊区，一排放着硬壳合订本，书脊上印着年份。 She published her first paper in a medical journal last spring.
sceneCN: 这里 journal 是「期刊」（第 1 个义项：定期出版的专门刊物），句意为她去年春天在医学期刊上发表了第一篇论文。画面里的物件：图书馆、合订本、书脊。

pos.zh: 名词：期刊；杂志；日志；日记

derivatives.zh: 由 journal 加 -ist 构成，义为「新闻工作者」
由 journalist 加 -ism 构成，义为「新闻业；新闻学」
由 journalist 加 -ic 构成，义为「新闻业的」
由 journal 加 -ed 构成，义为「记入日志的」（英式双写 l）

senses.title: A periodical on a special subject
senses.definition: a periodical, often containing serious articles, published for a profession or field
senses.definitionCN: 为某一行业或领域出版的定期刊物，多载严肃文章
senses.example: Her study appeared in a well-known journal.
senses.exampleCN: 她的研究发表在一份知名期刊上。
senses.why: The periodical sense grew out of the idea of something issued day by day.
senses.whyCN: 期刊义是从「按日发行」这个概念长出来的。

senses.title: A daily newspaper
senses.definition: a newspaper published every day, now mostly in formal or older usage
senses.definitionCN: 每天出版的报纸，现在多用于正式或较早的语境
senses.example: The news was read aloud from the local journal.
senses.exampleCN: 这条消息是从当地日报上念出来的。
senses.why: A newspaper issued every day takes its name straight from the daily book.
senses.whyCN: 日报每天发行，名字直接来自「每日的簿册」。

senses.title: A personal daily record
senses.definition: a book in which a person writes down events and thoughts each day
senses.definitionCN: 每天记下事情与想法的本子
senses.example: She has kept a journal since she was ten.
senses.exampleCN: 她十岁起就记日记。
senses.why: The oldest layer of the word is a book kept day by day by one person.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最古老的一层，是一个人按天记下的本子。

senses.title: A log of an activity
senses.definition: an official record of what is done, as in a ship or a laboratory
senses.definitionCN: 对所做之事的正式记录，如船上或实验室的记录
senses.example: The engineer noted the fault in the engine journal.
senses.exampleCN: 工程师把这个故障记在了轮机日志里。
senses.why: A ship or a lab keeps the same day book, but for duty rather than feeling.
senses.whyCN: 船上或实验室也记同样的日簿，只是记的是职责而不是心情。

senses.title: A published volume of papers
senses.definition: a volume collecting the proceedings or papers of a learned society
senses.definitionCN: 汇集某学会会议记录或论文的册子
senses.example: The society prints its journal every quarter.
senses.exampleCN: 该学会每季度印行自己的汇编。
senses.why: Issuing papers at fixed dates turns a day book into a journal for a whole field.
senses.whyCN: 按固定日期印行论文，把日簿变成面向整个领域的期刊。

senses.title: A travel account
senses.definition: a written account of travels, usually kept day by day
senses.definitionCN: 通常按天记录下来的行旅文字
senses.example: His travel journal became a small book.
senses.exampleCN: 他的旅行日志后来成了一本小书。
senses.why: Travellers keep the same daily habit, so the word follows them on the road.
senses.whyCN: 旅人保留同样的按天记录习惯，这个词就跟着他们上路。

intro.en: Journal comes from French journal, a daily book, which descends from Latin diurnalis, "of the day".
intro.cn: journal 来自法语 journal「每日的书」，其源头是拉丁语 diurnalis「每日的」。

items.en: diurnus meant of the day, from dies, a day.
items.cn: diurnus 意为「白日的」，源自 dies「日」。

items.en: diurnalis was the adjective built on diurnus.
items.cn: diurnalis 是由 diurnus 构成的形容词。

items.en: Old French journal meant daily, and also a daily record or book.
items.cn: 古法语 journal 既指「每日的」，也指每日的记录或簿册。

items.en: English adopted journal for a daily account and later for a newspaper.
items.cn: 英语借入 journal 指每日记述，后来又指报纸。

items.en: The learned periodical sense became dominant in the eighteenth century.
items.cn: 学术期刊义在十八世纪占据主导。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the journal stem; the near-meaning group holds other periodicals and records.
note.cn: 形近组共用 journal 词干；近义组收其他刊物与记录。

entries.definition: A person who writes for newspapers or broadcast.
entries.definitionCN: 由 journal 加 -ist 构成，指新闻工作者。

entries.definition: The work or study of news reporting.
entries.definitionCN: 派生名词，义为「新闻业；新闻学」。

entries.definition: A trip from one place to another.
entries.definitionCN: 拼写相近，义为「旅程」，源自同一拉丁「日」词根但路线不同。

entries.definition: A magazine published at regular intervals.
A book of daily personal notes.
entries.definitionCN: 指个人的日记本，更私人。

entries.definition: An official record of events.
entries.definitionCN: 技术上指正式运行记录。

normalIntro.en: These hooks move from Latin dies, a day, to the library shelf of bound volumes.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从拉丁语的「日」走到图书馆那排合订本。

normal.en: The root is dies, day, also seen in diary and diurnal.
normal.cn: 词根是 dies「日」，也见于 diary 与 diurnal。

normal.en: Journalist adds -ist to the periodical noun.
normal.cn: journalist 是给期刊名词加 -ist。

normal.en: Keep a journal is the personal use, at home.
normal.cn: keep a journal 是家里的私人用法。

normal.en: An academic journal is the professional use.
normal.cn: academic journal 是专业领域的用法。

normal.en: Jour and dies both survive in French and Latin day words.
normal.cn: 法语 jour 与拉丁 dies 都是「日」的词。

abstract.en: A journal is a day pressed flat into pages.
abstract.cn: 期刊就是把一天压平成纸页。

abstract.en: The same word holds a scholar and a schoolgirl.
abstract.cn: 同一个词既装着学者也装着女学生。

abstract.en: Bound volumes are years standing on a shelf.
abstract.cn: 合订本就是站在书架上的一整年。

examples.en: The journal publishes four issues a year.
examples.cn: 这本期刊一年出四期。

examples.en: He writes in his journal before sleep.
examples.cn: 他睡前写日志。

examples.en: Her article appeared in an academic journal.
examples.cn: 她的文章登在一份学术期刊上。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「 jour 日」加「nal」—— 每天一页，就是日志

root: 拉丁语 dies「日」→ diurnus「白日的」→ diurnalis → 古法语 journal「每日的；日志」→ 英语 journal。同族 diary、journalist、journey。

sensesIntro.en: Six senses: a specialist periodical, a daily paper, a personal diary, a log, a society volume, and a travel account.
sensesIntro.cn: 六个义项：专业期刊、日报、个人日记、运行日志、学会汇编，以及旅行游记。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: pages bound by dates, one day after another.
core.cn: 核心意象：按日期订起来的纸页，一天接一天。

branches.en: THE LIBRARY SHELF: issues bound into yearly volumes.
branches.cn: 书架这条线：各期合订成年卷。

branches.en: THE NEWS STAND: a paper that comes every morning.
branches.cn: 报摊这条线：每天早上来的报纸。

branches.en: THE DESK DRAWER: a private day book and a travel tale.
branches.cn: 抽屉这条线：私人的日记与行旅记述。

branches.en: THE ENGINE ROOM: an official log of faults.
branches.cn: 轮机舱这条线：正式记录的故障。

branches.en: THE PEER REVIEW: the gate where research is published.
branches.cn: 同行评议这条线：研究发表的关口。

intro.en: Journal carries the Latin day root di- and takes English endings for its family.
intro.cn: journal 带着拉丁「日」词根 di-，词族由英语词尾扩展。

latinIntro.en: The Latin relatives come from dies, a day, through diurnalis.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁同族词经由 diurnalis 来自 dies「日」。

definition_zh: 化合物；复合物；复合词；复合的；使加重
definition_en: a substance or thing made of two or more parts, or to make a problem worse
core_image: 两种粉末倒进同一只碗里，搅成一种新东西
scene: 实验室里，两种液体混合后颜色立刻变深。 The compound turned dark as soon as the two liquids met.
sceneCN: 这里 compound 指「化合物」（第 1 个义项：由两种以上元素化合成的物质）；句意是两种液体一相遇，这种化合物立刻变暗。

senses.title: A substance of joined elements
senses.definition: a substance formed when two or more elements join chemically
senses.definitionCN: 两种或更多元素经化学结合形成的物质
senses.example: Water is a compound of hydrogen and oxygen.
senses.exampleCN: 水是氢和氧的化合物。
senses.why: Chemistry shows that simple elements can join and lose their separate natures.
senses.whyCN: 化学证明简单元素能结合，并失去各自原来的性质。

senses.title: A thing of joined parts
senses.definition: something made by combining two or more parts
senses.definitionCN: 由两个或更多部分组合而成的事物
senses.example: Blackboard is a compound of black and board.
senses.exampleCN: blackboard 是 black 与 board 组合成的复合词。
senses.why: Language and buildings alike can be built by joining simple units.
senses.whyCN: 语言和建筑一样，都能靠连接简单单位来搭建。

senses.title: Make a problem worse
senses.definition: to make a bad situation or difficulty worse
senses.definitionCN: 使糟糕的处境或困难变得更严重
senses.example: Delay only compounded the damage.
senses.exampleCN: 拖延只会让损失加重。
senses.why: One harm added to another is a kind of chemical joining of troubles.
senses.whyCN: 一种伤害叠加到另一种上，就像麻烦的化合。

intro.en: Compound comes from Latin componere, to put together, and reached English through Old French compondre.
intro.cn: compound 来自拉丁语 componere（放在一起），经古法语 compondre 进入英语。

items.en: Componere meant to place several things together.
items.cn: componere 意为把几样东西放在一起。

items.en: Compositum named a thing built from separate parts.
items.cn: compositum 指由分开的部分构成的东西。

items.en: Old French compondre used the word for mixed substances.
items.cn: 古法语 compondre 用它指混合而成的物质。

items.en: English compound first described a mixture or a joined word.
items.cn: 英语 compound 最初指混合物或合成的词。

items.en: The verb sense of making trouble worse came later.
items.cn: 表示使麻烦加重的动词义项是后来出现的。

note.en: The look-alike group holds words close in shape to compound, and the meaning group names other mixtures and joined things.

definition_zh: 水库；蓄水池；储备
definition_en: a lake or container for storing water, or a large supply of something
core_image: 山谷被一道坝拦住，雨水在谷底静静积成一片湖
scene: 这座水库供应着下游三个城镇的饮用水。 The reservoir supplies drinking water to three towns downstream.
sceneCN: 这里 reservoir 是「水库」（第 1 个义项：蓄水的人工湖）；句意：这座水库为下游三个城镇供应饮用水。

senses.title: An artificial lake for water
senses.definition: a natural or artificial lake used for storing water for a town or region
senses.definitionCN: 为城镇或地区储水而建的自然或人工湖
senses.example: The reservoir supplies drinking water to three towns.
senses.exampleCN: 这座水库为三个城镇供应饮用水。
senses.why: The French noun names a place where something is kept, and water is the first thing stored there.
senses.whyCN: 这个法语名词指储存某物的地方，而水是最先被储存在那里的东西。

senses.title: A large supply of something
senses.definition: a large amount of something available when needed, such as knowledge or talent
senses.definitionCN: 需要时可取用的大量某物，如知识或人才
senses.example: She has a deep reservoir of patience.
senses.exampleCN: 她有很深的耐心储备。
senses.why: Water kept in reserve becomes a metaphor for any resource held in large quantity.
senses.whyCN: 蓄起来的水，成为任何大量储备资源的比喻。

senses.title: A container that holds fluid
senses.definition: a container inside a machine that holds ink, oil, or another fluid
senses.definitionCN: 机器内部盛放墨水、油或其他液体的容器

senses.exampleCN: 钢笔的墨盒空了。
senses.why: The same storage image shrinks to a small part inside a tool.
senses.whyCN: 同样的储存意象缩小为工具内部的一个小部件。

normal.en: The -oir ending in French often names a place or container.

abstract.cn: 想象大坝挡住一堵绿色的水墙。

abstract.en: Think of a deep well no one can see the bottom of.

sensesIntro.en: The word names a place of storage: first a lake for water, then any large supply held ready, then a small container inside a tool.

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a valley sealed by a dam, holding water in reserve.

branches.en: A water lake is the basic physical sense.
branches.cn: 蓄水的湖，是基本物理义项。

branches.en: Any large supply is water turned into metaphor.
branches.cn: 任何大量储备，都是「水」的比喻化。

branches.en: A reservoir stores for a town, just as knowledge stores for a person.
branches.cn: 水库为城镇储存，知识为人储存。

branches.en: Large supplies and small ink supplies are both held in reserve.

definition_zh: 经济衰退；后退；退去
definition_en: a period when trade and industry shrink; the act of moving back; the slow withdrawal of water or ice
core_image: 退潮后的沙滩上留下一道道水痕
scene: 工厂车间贴出停工通知，工人排队走出大门。 Many factories closed during the recession.
sceneCN: 这里 recession 是「经济衰退」（第 1 个义项：工商业萎缩的时期）；句意为许多工厂在衰退期间倒闭。画面里可留意：停工的车间、贴出的通知。

senses.title: A shrinking economy
senses.definition: a period in which trade, industry, and output fall for several months
senses.definitionCN: 贸易、工业与产出连续数月下滑的时期
senses.example: Many factories closed during the recession.
senses.exampleCN: 许多工厂在衰退期间倒闭。
senses.why: An economy that goes backward is pictured as a tide going out, and the noun for that backward movement became the name of the slump.
senses.whyCN: 往回走的经济被描绘成退潮，而表这种后退的名词成了萧条的称呼。

senses.title: The act of moving back
senses.definition: the act of withdrawing or stepping back from a position
senses.definitionCN: 从某一位置撤回或后退的行为
senses.example: The army's recession from the border was orderly.
senses.exampleCN: 军队从边境的后撤井然有序。
senses.why: Latin recedere means to go back, and the noun kept the plain physical sense before economics borrowed it.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 recedere 意为往回走，名词先保留了这个朴素的物理义，后来才被经济学借用。

senses.title: The slow withdrawal of water or ice
senses.definition: the gradual movement back of a tide, a glacier, or a flood
senses.definitionCN: 潮水、冰川或洪水的逐渐回退
senses.example: The recession of the glacier exposed bare rock.
senses.exampleCN: 冰川的退去露出了裸露的岩石。
senses.why: Water and ice going back are the same movement as an army going back, so the word covers natural withdrawal.
senses.whyCN: 水与冰的回退，和军队的后撤是同一种运动，因此这个词也涵盖自然的退去。

intro.en: Recession is a Latin going-back noun: first a step backward, then a tide, then a whole economy.
intro.cn: recession 是拉丁语表「往回走」的名词：先是后退一步，再是退潮，最后是整个经济。

items.en: Cedere meant to go or yield, the movement at the heart of the family.
items.cn: cedere 意为走或让出，是整个词族的核心动作。

items.en: Recedere added re-, back, to cedere, giving the sense of going backward.
items.cn: recedere 在 cedere 前加 re-（回），得到「往回走」的意思。

items.en: Recessus, the noun of the verb, named a backward movement or a withdrawn place.
items.cn: 动词的名词形式 recessus 指后退的运动或退隐之处。

items.en: French recession carried the noun into English with its physical sense intact.
items.cn: 法语 récession 把这个名词带入英语，物理义完好保留。

items.en: In the twentieth century the word became the standard term for a shrinking economy.
items.cn: 二十世纪，这个词成为经济萎缩的标准术语。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers nouns ending in the same sound; the near-meaning group gathers words for economic decline.
note.cn: 形近组收结尾音相同的名词；近义组收表经济下滑的词。

normalIntro.en: The word is a going back: first a tide, then an army, then the whole economy.

normal.en: Re plus cess plus ion: going back again and again.
normal.cn: re 加 cess 加 ion：一再往回走。

normal.en: Recession and recede share the same going-back root.
normal.cn: recession 与 recede 共享同一个「往回走」的词根。

normal.en: An economy in recession is a tide going out.
normal.cn: 处于衰退的经济，就是正在退去的潮水。

normal.en: Economic recession is the most common modern use.
normal.cn: economic recession 是当代最常见的用法。

normal.en: Two c and two s in succession: recession is easy to misspell.
normal.cn: succession 里有两个 c 两个 s，recession 也容易拼错。

abstract.en: A recession is a society discovering what it cannot afford.
abstract.cn: 衰退是一个社会发现自己负担不起什么的过程。

abstract.en: What goes out with the tide leaves marks that show where it stood.
abstract.cn: 随潮退去的东西会留下痕迹，标出它曾经的位置。

abstract.en: Every retreat is also a chance to see the ground clearly.
abstract.cn: 每一次后退，也是看清地面的机会。

examples.en: Many factories closed during the recession.
examples.cn: 许多工厂在衰退期间倒闭。

examples.en: The recession of the glacier exposed bare rock.
examples.cn: 冰川的退去露出了裸露的岩石。

examples.en: The company survived two recessions in a decade.
examples.cn: 这家公司在十年里挺过了两次衰退。

dict_mnemonic.text: re（回）加 cess（走）加 ion（行为）：往回走就是后退；整个经济往回走，就是衰退。

root: 拉丁 cedere（走）→ recedere（往回走）→ recessus（后退）→ 法语 récession → 英语 recession；同族有 recede、recess、recessive。

sensesIntro.en: The core is movement backward; the senses move from an army stepping back to a tide withdrawing and to a shrinking economy.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「向后退」；义项从军队后撤，到潮水退去，再到经济萎缩。

branches.en: a closed factory gate
branches.cn: 关上的工厂大门

branches.en: a line of soldiers stepping back
branches.cn: 一列士兵向后退

branches.en: a glacier leaving bare rock
branches.cn: 冰川退去露出岩石

branches.en: a retreat and a shrinking economy
branches.cn: 撤退与萎缩的经济

branches.en: an army and a tide both going back
branches.cn: 军队与潮水一同后退

intro.en: A Latin verb of going takes a prefix of return and a noun ending, and the family spreads from footsteps to markets.
intro.cn: 拉丁语的「走」动词接上表「回」的前缀与名词词尾，这个词族从脚步延伸到市场。

latinIntro.en: The Latin base is cedere, to go; re- turns it back, and -io makes the movement a noun.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁词根是 cedere（走）；re- 使其转向回，-io 把这一运动变成名词。

definition_zh: 突出的；显眼的；著名的；显要的；重要的；（特征）显著的；（结构）外凸的
definition_en: standing out from a surface or from other people, and therefore easy to notice or important
core_image: 一块石头从墙面上凸出来，走过的人都先看见它
scene: 她的名字出现在海报最显眼的位置。 A prominent sandstone arch frames the entrance to the old library.
sceneCN: 这里 prominent 是「向外突出的」（第 3 个义项：结构从墙面伸出、形成门框）；句意：一道突出的砂岩拱券框住了老图书馆的入口。图中可辨识物件：从墙面伸出的拱券、被框住的入口；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: 突出的；显眼的；著名的；显要的；显著的

senses.title: Well known and respected
senses.definition: widely known and respected in a particular field
senses.definitionCN: 在某一领域广为人知并受敬重
senses.example: A prominent economist warned that the housing boom would end.
senses.exampleCN: 一位著名经济学家警告说房地产繁荣将会结束。
senses.why: Prominens meant 'standing out'. Fame is social standing out: the person rises visibly above the ordinary level of the profession.
senses.whyCN: prominens 意为“突出的”。名声就是社会意义上的突出：这个人明显高出于行业的一般水平。

senses.title: Holding an important position
senses.definition: having an important or influential position in an organization or society
senses.definitionCN: 在组织或社会中居于重要或有影响力的位置
senses.example: Several prominent families opposed the new tax.
senses.exampleCN: 几个显赫家族反对这项新税。
senses.why: The word moves from visibility to power: a prominent family is one whose name stands out in public affairs and can therefore sway them.
senses.whyCN: 这个词从可见度转到权力：显赫家族的名字在公共事务中突出，因此能左右事务。

senses.title: Sticking out from a surface
senses.definition: rising or projecting above the surrounding surface
senses.definitionCN: 高出或伸出周围表面的
senses.example: The old house had prominent stone arches over every window.
senses.exampleCN: 这座老房子每扇窗上都有突出的石拱。
senses.why: This is the literal core: the thing itself pushes forward beyond the plane it belongs to, so it catches the eye before anything else.
senses.whyCN: 这是字面核心：事物本身顶出所属平面之外，所以比其他东西更早抓住视线。

senses.title: Impossible to overlook
senses.titleCN: 一眼就能看到、难以忽略
senses.definition: placed or shaped so that it is noticed immediately
senses.definitionCN: 放置或造型使其立刻被注意到
senses.example: The safety instructions were printed in a prominent band of red.
senses.exampleCN: 安全说明被印在一条醒目的红色带子上。
senses.why: When designers call a label prominent, they mean it wins the competition for attention against everything around it.
senses.whyCN: 当设计师说某个标签 prominent，意思是它在与周围一切争夺注意力时胜出。

senses.title: Clearly visible in a feature
senses.definition: clearly marked or easily observed, as of a sign or symptom
senses.definitionCN: 指迹象或症状明显、易于观察
senses.example: The first prominent symptom was a persistent dry cough.
senses.exampleCN: 最先出现的明显症状是持续干咳。
senses.why: In medicine the word marks what a clinician cannot miss: a sign that presents itself plainly rather than hiding in the background.
senses.whyCN: 在医学中，这个词标记临床医生不会漏掉的东西：一个直接呈现、不藏在背景里的征象。

senses.title: The leading element
senses.definition: the most important or noticeable element among several
senses.definitionCN: 若干要素中最重要或最引人注意的一个
senses.example: Loss of trust is the most prominent theme in the interviews.
senses.exampleCN: 失去信任是这些访谈中最突出的主题。
senses.why: Among competing elements, the prominent one is the one that stands above the rest of the set, much as a bump stands above a surface.
senses.whyCN: 在相互竞争的要素中，突出的那一个是高出其余部分的，就像凸起高出表面。

senses.title: Socially conspicuous
senses.definition: attracting public notice because of wealth, rank or family name
senses.definitionCN: 因财富、地位或家族名望而引人注目
senses.example: The wedding was attended by the town's most prominent citizens.
senses.exampleCN: 镇上最显要的市民都出席了这场婚礼。
senses.why: The social sense specializes in public notice: not merely famous for work, but visible because of rank or wealth.
senses.whyCN: 社会义专门指向公众注意：不仅因工作而出名，更因地位或财富而显眼。

senses.title: Standing out to the eye or ear
senses.definition: visually or acoustically strong enough to dominate the surrounding pattern
senses.definitionCN: 在视觉或听觉上足够强，压过周围的图案或声音
senses.example: A prominent blue stripe runs through the whole fabric.
senses.exampleCN: 一道醒目的蓝色条纹贯穿整块布料。
senses.why: Design and music use the word for the element that dominates the pattern, whether a colour or a beat.
senses.whyCN: 设计与音乐用这个词指压过整体图案的元素，无论是一种颜色还是一个节拍。

intro.en: Prominent is the present participle of Latin prominere, 'to stand out, to project'. Pro- gives the forward push and minere gives the jutting. English borrowed it in the 17th century and let it spread from rocks and bones to reputations, symptoms and design.
intro.cn: prominent 是拉丁 prominere“突出、外伸”的现在分词。pro- 提供向前的推力，minere 提供“伸出”。英语在 17 世纪借入，并让它从岩石与骨骼扩展到名声、症状与设计。

items.en: Minere meant 'to jut or overhang'. Its deeper origin is uncertain; connections with eminere and imminere are generally accepted, while a link to mons 'mountain' remains unproved.
items.cn: minere 意为“伸出、悬突”，更深来源不确定；与 eminere、imminere 的关联一般被接受，而与 mons“山”的联系尚未证实。

items.en: Prominere combined pro- 'forward' with minere 'jut' and meant 'to stand out, to project'. Its participle prominens described whatever was doing the standing out.
items.cn: prominere 由 pro-“向前”与 minere“伸出”组成，意为“突出、外伸”。其分词 prominens 描述正在突出的东西。

items.en: The participle was already used for projecting parts of buildings and bodies, so the adjective carried a physical meaning from the start.
items.cn: 这个分词已用于建筑与身体的外凸部位，因此形容词从一开始就带有物理含义。

items.en: English adopted prominent for physical projections first, then extended it to anything that stood above its surroundings in importance.
items.cn: 英语先借 prominent 指物理凸起，再扩展到任何在重要性上高出周围环境的事物。

items.en: Newspapers made 'prominent citizens' a familiar phrase, and the adjective became the standard word for public standing.
items.cn: 报纸使“显要市民”成为常见说法，这个形容词也成为表示公共地位的标准词。

items.en: Clinical writing adopted prominent for signs that stand out, while design and music used it for elements that dominate a pattern.
items.cn: 临床写作采用 prominent 指明显的征象，设计与音乐则用它指压过整体图案的元素。

note.en: The look-alike group separates the adjective from its noun, adverb and the eminence family. The meaning group contrasts being famous, being obvious and being physically raised.
note.cn: 形近组区分形容词与它的名词、副词形式及 eminence 词族；词义组比较“有名”“明显”与“物理凸起”。

entries.definition: the quality of standing out, or the raised part itself. It names what prominent describes.
entries.definitionCN: 突出的性质，或凸起本身。它命名 prominent 所描述的东西。

entries.definition: in a way that is easy to notice. It tells how something is placed or shown.
entries.definitionCN: 以容易注意的方式。它说明某物如何被放置或展示。

entries.definition: high rank or a height. It comes from eminere, the same jutting verb with e- 'out' instead of pro- 'forward'.
entries.definitionCN: 高位或高地。它来自 eminere，同一个“伸出”动词，只是用 e-“向外”取代 pro-“向前”。

entries.definition: lasting forever. It looks similar but comes from per- 'through' plus manere 'to remain', a completely different root.
entries.definitionCN: 永久的。它看起来相似，却来自 per-“贯穿”加 manere“停留”，词根完全不同。

entries.definition: distinguished and highly respected. It is close to sense 01 but sounds more formal and more about rank.
entries.definitionCN: 卓越且深受敬重的。它接近第 1 义项，但更正式、更强调等级。

entries.definition: clearly visible, often because of unusual appearance. It stresses being seen, while prominent stresses standing above a level.
entries.definitionCN: 明显可见的，常因外形不寻常。它强调被看见，而 prominent 强调高出某一水平。

entries.definition: easy to see or feel. It is the plain everyday word for sense 04.
entries.definitionCN: 容易看到或感觉到的。它是第 4 义项的日常说法。

entries.definition: sticking out physically. It is the narrow word for sense 03, with no fame or importance attached.
entries.definitionCN: 物理上伸出的。它是第 3 义项的窄义说法，不附带名声或重要性。

normalIntro.en: These hooks pin the word to one raised shape, then let it travel from walls to faces, from symptoms to fame.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩把词钉在一个隆起的形状上，再让它从墙面走到面孔、从症状走到名声。

normal.en: Split it as pro + min + ent: forward + jut + adjective. Anything that juts forward is prominent.
normal.cn: 拆成 pro + min + ent：向前、伸出、形容词。凡是向前伸出的就是 prominent。

normal.en: Picture a wall with one brick pushed out: your hand finds that brick first.
normal.cn: 想象一面墙里有一块砖被顶了出来：你的手最先摸到那块砖。

normal.en: Prominent teeth and a prominent nose are the same brick, moved to a face.
normal.cn: 突出的牙齿与高鼻梁就是同一块砖，被移到了脸上。

normal.en: A prominent symptom is the brick in a medical chart: the one the doctor circles.
normal.cn: 明显症状就是病历里的那块砖：医生会把它圈出来。

normal.en: A prominent scientist is the same brick in a crowd: the one the reporters call first.
normal.cn: 著名科学家就是人群里的那块砖：记者最先打电话给他。

abstract.en: The word always needs a background: a bump on a bump is not prominent, only a bump on a flat surface is.
abstract.cn: 这个词始终需要背景：凸起上的凸起并不突出，只有平面上的凸起才突出。

abstract.en: Keep fame and shape in one frame: the person stands out socially exactly as the brick stands out physically.
abstract.cn: 把名声与形状放在同一个框架里：人在社会上突出，正如砖头在物理上突出。

abstract.en: Watch the suffix: prominent describes, prominence names, prominently tells how.
abstract.cn: 留意后缀：prominent 描述，prominence 命名，prominently 说明方式。

examples.en: A prominent legal scholar argued that the ruling was too broad.
examples.cn: 一位著名法学学者主张该判决范围过宽。

examples.en: The bird's most prominent feature is the bright red crest on its head.
examples.cn: 这种鸟最显著的特征是头顶鲜红的冠羽。

examples.en: Warning signs were mounted in prominent positions along the cliff path.
examples.cn: 警示牌被安装在悬崖步道的显眼位置。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音“扑罗米能特”：一块米能特别突出，从平面上顶出来。

root: 拉丁 prominere 的现在分词 prominens“突出的”（pro- 向前 + minere 伸出）；核心是“从平面顶出来、一眼看见”。

sensesIntro.en: The eight senses all describe one thing standing above another: a scholar above peers, a family above society, a stone above a wall, a label above text, a symptom above silence, a theme above its rivals, a citizen above the town, a stripe above the fabric.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都在描述一物高出另一物：学者高出同行，家族高出社会，石头高出墙面，标签压过文字，症状压过沉默，主题压过其他主题，市民高出小镇，条纹压过布料。

core.en: A part that rises above its background, so that attention lands on it before anything else.
core.cn: 一部分高出背景，因此注意力先落在它上面。

branches.en: PEOPLE: a person rises above peers by reputation or position.
branches.cn: 人：一个人凭名声或地位高出同侪。

branches.en: SHAPE: a part pushes out of its surface and dominates the pattern.
branches.cn: 形状：一部分顶出表面，压过整体图案。

branches.en: VISIBILITY: what stands out is noticed at once, in a room or on a chart.
branches.cn: 可见度：突出的东西立刻被注意到，无论在房间里还是在图表上。

branches.en: COMPETITION: among rival elements, one stands above the rest of the set.
branches.cn: 竞争：在相互竞争的要素中，有一个高出其余。

branches.en: SOCIETY: rank and wealth make a family visible in public life.
branches.cn: 社会：地位与财富让一个家族在公共生活中显眼。

intro.en: Prominent is a Latin participle used as an adjective. The items below show the same jutting verb through noun, adverb and the sibling prefixes e- and in-.
intro.cn: prominent 是拉丁分词用作形容词。下列条目沿着同一个“伸出”动词，走过名词、副词与同胞前缀 e-、in-。

latinIntro.en: The Latin entries give the verb and its participle. They explain why prominent, prominence and eminence keep the same core image.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语条目给出动词与分词，解释为什么 prominent、prominence 与 eminence 保持同一个核心意象。

items.example: A prominent ridge hides the valley from view.
items.exampleCN: 一道突出的山脊挡住了山谷的视线。

items.meaning: the state of standing out; a bump
items.example: The tower's prominence makes it a landmark.
items.exampleCN: 这座塔的突出使它成为地标。

items.example: The flag was prominently hung above the door.
items.exampleCN: 旗帜显眼地挂在门上方。

items.example: The hill's eminence gives a view of the bay.
items.exampleCN: 这座山丘的高起让人能看到海湾。

items.example: An eminent critic praised the first novel.
items.exampleCN: 一位著名评论家称赞了这部处女作。
锈蚀表明随时可能坍塌。

items.example: His reputation was supereminent in his lifetime.

items.exampleCN: 这个计划非常切实可行。

definition_zh: 承认；让步；让出；失球
definition_en: to admit that something is true, or to allow someone to have something
core_image: 棋手把王轻轻推倒，抬手示意这一局认输
scene: 争论到最后，他点头承认对方说得有道理。 He finally conceded that she had a point.
sceneCN: 这里 concede 指「承认」（第 1 个义项：不情愿地承认某事属实）；句意是他最后承认她说的有道理。

senses.title: Admit something is true
senses.definition: to admit that something is true, often unwillingly
senses.definitionCN: 常常不情愿地承认某事属实
senses.example: She conceded that the plan had failed.
senses.exampleCN: 她承认这个计划失败了。
senses.why: To concede is to stop resisting a fact you can no longer deny.
senses.whyCN: 承认就是停止抵抗一个再也无法否认的事实。

senses.title: Hand over a right
senses.definition: to allow someone to have something you held
senses.definitionCN: 允许别人得到你原本拥有的东西
senses.example: The company conceded two seats on the board.
senses.exampleCN: 公司让出了董事会的两个席位。
senses.why: The older sense is yielding ground, and ground can be a seat or a right.
senses.whyCN: 更古老的意思是让出地盘，而地盘也可以是席位或权利。

senses.title: Allow the other side to score
senses.definition: to allow the opposing team to score a goal or point
senses.definitionCN: 让对方球队攻入一球或得到一分
senses.example: The team conceded a goal in the last minute.
senses.exampleCN: 球队在最后一分钟失了一球。
senses.why: In sport you yield a point the way an army yields ground.
senses.whyCN: 在运动里让掉一分，就像军队让出阵地。

intro.en: Concede comes from Latin concedere, to go away or give way, built from com-, together, and cedere, to go.
intro.cn: concede 来自拉丁语 concedere（走开、让路），由 com-（一起）与 cedere（走）构成。

items.en: Cedere meant to go, to yield or to withdraw.
items.cn: cedere 意为走、让出或退去。

items.en: Concedere meant to give way or to grant a request.
items.cn: concedere 意为让路或应允请求。

items.en: French concéder kept the sense of granting and yielding.
items.cn: 法语 concéder 保留了应允与让出的意思。

items.en: English concede first meant to grant or to admit.
items.cn: 英语 concede 最初指准许或承认。

items.en: Sport added the sense of letting the other side score.
items.cn: 体育又加上了让对方得分的意思。

note.en: The look-alike group holds words close in shape to concede, and the meaning group names other words for admitting or yielding.
note.cn: 形近组收的是与 concede 形状相近的词，近义组列出其他表示承认与让出的词。

entries.definition: to form an idea in the mind
to hide something
to come before something else
to agree that something is true
to agree to give something
to give way under pressure

normalIntro.en: These hooks begin with a chess king tipped over, then move to yielding ground and to a lost goal.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子从被推倒的棋子王开始，再走到让出阵地与失球。

normal.en: Con- is together and cede is to go, so to concede is to go away from your own claim.
normal.cn: con- 是一起，cede 是走，concede 就是从自己的主张上退开。

normal.en: To concede a point is to let the other side keep it.
normal.cn: 承认对方一点，就是让对方保住那一点。

normal.en: Concede and cede share the idea of giving ground.
normal.cn: concede 与 cede 都带有让出地盘的意思。

normal.en: A team that concedes a goal has allowed it, not scored it.
normal.cn: 球队 concede 一球，是让对方进球，不是自己进。

normal.en: Concession is the noun, the thing given away.
normal.cn: concession 是名词，即被让出去的东西。

abstract.en: Picture a chess player laying the king on its side.
abstract.cn: 想象棋手把王侧放在棋盘上。

abstract.en: Picture one side of a tug of war letting go of the rope.
abstract.cn: 想象拔河的一方松开绳子。

abstract.en: Picture a hand opening to release a held coin.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手摊开，放走握着的一枚硬币。

examples.en: He conceded that he had made a mistake.
examples.cn: 他承认自己犯了错。

examples.en: The government conceded several demands.
examples.cn: 政府让步，答应了若干要求。

examples.en: The team conceded twice in the second half.
examples.cn: 球队在下半场失了两球。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 concede 记成 con（一起）加 cede（走）：从自己的立场上退开一步，就是让步、承认。

root: 源自拉丁语 concedere（com 一起 + cedere 走），本义是走开、让路，后引申为让出权利、承认事实与在比赛中失球。

sensesIntro.en: From stepping aside, to admitting a fact, and finally to letting the other side score.
sensesIntro.cn: 从让到一边，到承认一个事实，最后到让对方得分。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a chess player tipping the king over to end the game.
core.cn: 核心意象：棋手把王推倒，结束这一局。

branches.en: Admitting a fact is the most common modern sense.
branches.cn: 承认事实是最常见的现代义项。

branches.en: Giving up a right is the older, more physical sense.
branches.cn: 让出权利是更古老、更具体的义项。

branches.en: Sport borrows the same picture of yielding ground.
branches.cn: 体育借用了同一幅让出地盘的画面。

branches.en: Admitting and granting both lower your own claim.
branches.cn: 承认与给予都降低了自己的主张。

branches.en: A seat and a goal are both things you let go.
branches.cn: 席位和进球都是你放手让出的东西。

intro.en: Concede is built on Latin com-, together, plus cedere, to go or yield.
intro.cn: concede 由拉丁语 com-（一起）与 cedere（走、让）构成。

latinIntro.en: The Latin go base ced- also gives proceed, recede and access.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语的行走词基 ced- 还给出 proceed、recede 与 access。

items.example: He concedes that the evidence is strong.
The seat was conceded without a fight.
items.exampleCN: 那个席位未经争夺就让出了。
她笑了笑，却没有让出任何东西。

items.example: The clause begins with a concessive word.
items.exampleCN: 这个从句以一个让步词开头。

items.example: He was the first conceder in the debate.
items.exampleCN: 他是辩论中第一个让步的人。

items.example: It is concededly a difficult task.

definition_zh: 卷心菜；甘蓝；钞票
definition_en: a large round vegetable with thick leaves packed in layers
core_image: 菜地里层层包裹的圆球
scene: 菜市场堆着刚摘的青菜。 She bought a cabbage for the soup.
sceneCN: 这里 cabbage 是「卷心菜」（第 1 个义项：叶片层层包成球的蔬菜）；句意是她买了一个卷心菜煮汤。

derivatives.zh: 菜青虫，专吃卷心菜叶的幼虫
羽衣甘蓝，与卷心菜同属的蔬菜

senses.title: The layered green vegetable
senses.definition: a round vegetable with thick leaves wrapped around a firm heart
senses.definitionCN: 叶片层层层包住硬芯的圆形蔬菜
senses.example: She bought a cabbage for the soup.
senses.exampleCN: 她买了一个卷心菜煮汤。
senses.why: The core image is a head made of leaves folded over one another.
senses.whyCN: 核心意象是一颗由层层叶片包成的菜球。

senses.title: The whole cabbage family
senses.definition: the group of leafy plants that includes cabbage and kale
senses.definitionCN: 包括卷心菜和羽衣甘蓝在内的叶菜类群
senses.example: Farmers here grow several cabbages.
senses.exampleCN: 这里的农民种好几种甘蓝。
senses.why: One common member lent its name to the whole group.
senses.whyCN: 其中一个常见成员的名字，被用来指整个类群。

senses.title: Old slang for money
senses.definition: an old slang word for paper money
senses.definitionCN: 旧时俚语，指纸币
senses.example: He saved his cabbage for a rainy day.
senses.exampleCN: 他把钱存起来以备不时之需。
senses.why: Green banknotes were compared to the green leaves of the vegetable.
senses.whyCN: 绿色的纸币被比作这种蔬菜的绿叶。

intro.en: Cabbage goes back through French to a Latin word for head.
intro.cn: cabbage 经由法语，追溯到拉丁语里表示「头」的词。

items.en: caput meant the head.
items.cn: 拉丁语 caput 意为头。

items.en: caboche meant a head, including a leafy one.
items.cn: 古法语 caboche 指头，也可指叶球。

items.en: caboche named the leafy garden vegetable.
items.cn: 中古英语 caboche 指这种叶菜。

items.en: The spelling cabbage settled in English.
items.cn: 十六世纪拼写固定为 cabbage。

items.en: Cabbage names the vegetable, its family and old slang for money.
items.cn: 现代英语中 cabbage 指这种蔬菜、其类群以及旧俚语里的钱。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the cabbage base; the near-meaning group gives other leafy vegetables.
note.cn: 形近组共用 cabbage 词基；近义组是其他叶菜。

normal.en: The plural is cabbages.

normal.en: Red cabbage keeps its colour when pickled.

normal.en: Kale and broccoli are close relatives.

normal.en: Cabbage once meant paper money in slang.

abstract.en: See green notes folded like leaves.
